- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary
The report request list was fetched once, so a request that was still REQUESTED or PROCESSING kept that status until you reloaded the page. We now poll every 5 seconds while any listed request is still in progress and stop once none are. The interval is derived from the cached list rather than passed to SWR as a function: SWR puts a function interval in its effect deps, so every render of the consumer would re-arm the timer and keep pushing the next poll out.

`routes.json` also registered three extra pages. `overview` mounted a second copy of the Reports page at `/spa/overview`, and `scheduled-overview` and `reports-data-overview` referenced component names that `index.ts` never exported, so they logged `does not define a component called "scheduled-overview"` and rendered an empty page. The root `reports` page already serves those views through its own routes, so this removes the three entries and the two exports that only existed for them.

## Screenshots

The report moves from **Queued → Running → Completed** without a manual refresh. REST responses are simulated to make the lifecycle deterministic; the PR’s actual polling logic runs at five-second intervals. The capture also checks that requests stop after completion.

title: (fix) Keep the subscription form and report the error when saving fails
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary
Saving the subscription wrote the new values into the SWR cache optimistically and then checked `response.ok`. `openmrsFetch` rejects on any non-2xx, so that error branch was unreachable, and the optimistic write stored a bare subscription where `useSubscription` expects `{ data: { results: [...] } }`. On a failed save the hook read `undefined`, the effect blanked every input, nothing revalidated, and the only feedback was the framework's generic unhandled-error toast. Easy to hit: a URL with a typo in the scheme gets a 500 from the backend.

This drops the optimistic write and wraps the save in try/catch. On failure we show the app's own error notification with the server message and leave the inputs as typed. On success we revalidate and show the existing success message.

It also judges an import upload by its `.zip` extension instead of its MIME type. Browsers report ZIPs under any of the four types the backend accepts, or with no type at all, so the old check rejected valid archives on some platforms (related to OCLOMRS-1121). Accepting `application/octet-stream` alone would have let any unknown binary through with a message saying only .zip files are allowed, so the name check is the one that gates.

## Screenshots

A rejected subscription save displays the server’s reason and preserves the entered URL and token. The HTTP 400 response is simulated, and the token is a dummy demo value; no subscription is changed.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d4c80f71-38bc-460d-a382-2cf3674426c4

## Related Issue

## Other
Two save tests in `subscription.test.tsx`, skipped since 9853c65, pass under the current tooling, so they're un-skipped here.

The de and ru_RU translations of "New package" fall back to English until Transifex picks up the new key. `editPackage` was missing from en.json because it was only used in `metadata-package-form-utils.ts`, which the extractor doesn't scan. body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [ ] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

Cards on the system administration page jump around as they load. Each card comes from a different app and only renders once that app's code has loaded. The slot lays them out in a wrapping flex row, and a card's wrapper takes no space until the card renders, so each late card pushes the ones already on screen sideways or onto the next row. On a slow connection, the stock and billing cards render early and then get bumped to the second row as the cards before them fill in. I noticed this while profiling the page's load.

This PR gives each card's wrapper a minimum size that matches the rendered card plus its margins (15rem by 9rem), so every card is in its final position from the start.

This doesn't leave gaps for cards the user can't see. The framework drops extensions filtered out by privileges, feature flags, online/offline flags or display conditions before rendering them, so they never get a wrapper. All 11 current cards render a `ClickableTile` unconditionally. The one case that changes is a card whose code fails to load, which now leaves an empty space instead of collapsing.

## Screenshots

Before and after of a throttled cold load, recorded at 2x. "Before" is the same build with the new rule cancelled.

Styling `[data-extension-id]` from the slot's stylesheet is what the home app's [metrics row](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-home/blob/main/packages/esm-home-app/src/metrics/metrics.scss) does to size its metric cards.

## Summary

Adds `swr` to the reports app's `peerDependencies` so the build tooling federates it, and pins the exact `2.5.1` dependency the way the other packages in this repo already do, so the fallback copy matches the app shell.

The openmrs rspack config builds the module federation `shared` list from `peerDependencies`. The other four packages here declare `swr` as a peer; reports didn't, so `swr` only reached it transitively, the built entry registered no `swr` share, and it bundled a private copy. `useSWR` from that copy reads its own `SWRConfig` context, not the one the framework's component decorator provides, so the reports app has been running on SWR's stock defaults (revalidate on focus and reconnect, unlimited retries on every error) and its own cache rather than the shared one.

Verified by building and checking the remote entry, which now registers `swr`, `swr/_internal`, `swr/immutable` and `swr/infinite` at 2.5.1 like the sibling packages. Same change as openmrs/openmrs-esm-form-builder#1347, where the dev server run against dev3 showed the forms list stop refetching on window focus once the framework's `revalidateOnFocus: false` applied.

One source change rides along: the cancel modal refreshed the report tables through the global `mutate` imported from `swr`. That function is bound to SWR's default cache, while every hook rendered under the framework's component decorator lives in the decorator's provider cache. With the private copy the two coincided; once swr is shared the global `mutate` reaches nothing and the tables would not refresh after a cancel or delete (the laboratory app's e2e suite caught the same thing in openmrs/openmrs-esm-laboratory-app#844). The second commit takes `mutate` from `useSWRConfig()` instead, which is what patient-chart already does everywhere.

The compressed-size action builds the pull request and base revisions sequentially in the same workspace. body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number.
- [x] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below.
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

Follow-up to #311. The admin card is gated on `Manage Global Properties`, so users without it don't see the link. But the page route has no such gate, so a user with only `Get Global Properties` can reach `/visit-summary-config` by direct URL, where they previously saw a fully editable page whose every save was rejected with a snackbar that read like a backend fault rather than a permissions problem.

This makes the page detect that case and present read-only, using the in-component `useSession` + `userHasAccess` pattern from `esm-reports-app`.

## What this does

When the user can view but not save, every mutating control (section toggles, reorder arrows, Save, Save & preview) is disabled, with `!canSave` OR-ed in front of the existing disabled conditions so nothing else regresses. Save & preview is disabled too, since it saves before rendering. A non-dismissible `InlineNotification` (`kind="info"`) explains they can view but not change the settings and that saving needs Manage Global Properties.

This is deliberately distinct from the existing 403 state (`kind="error"`, "can't load this page at all"). Two different situations, two different messages. The page stays fully functional read-only: the sections list, saved order, and locked-section tooltips all still work.

No change to the backend, the resource layer, or routes. The privilege string matches `PrivilegeConstants.MANAGE_GLOBAL_PROPERTIES` and the value already gating the card in `routes.json`.

Save & preview is disabled read-only since it writes; a view-only preview button is out of scope. The idle placeholder still references Save & preview, left as-is since that button is simply disabled for these users.

## Screenshots

<!-- attach: (1) user WITH the privilege, controls live; (2) user without it, info notice + disabled controls -->

## Related Issue

https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-5848
Parent epic: https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-5667

## Tests

25 passing (18 existing, 7 new). No existing assertion weakened; the existing suite is pinned to a can-save user via the shared session mock so its assertions stand verbatim. New tests cover: the privilege checked with the exact string against the session user, the notice absent when the user can save, every mutating control disabled (asserting the reorder-arrow count so an ungated one fails), the read-only notice distinct from the 403 copy, the notice non-dismissible, sections still rendering read-only, and no write firing on toggle/Save/Save & preview.

## Summary
Adds a Visit Summary Configuration page under System Administration, in a new `esm-patient-documents-admin-app` package. Admins can see every visit summary section registered by the patientdocuments module, toggle sections on and off, reorder them, save, and preview the result.

The section list comes from `GET /ws/rest/v1/patientdocuments/visitSummary/sections`, so a downstream module's custom section appears automatically with no change here. Saving writes the existing global properties `report.visitSummary.section.<key>.enabled` and `.order` through the standard `systemsetting` REST resource, so there is no new write API. Sections the module marks as not toggleable (facility header, patient info, footer) render with a locked toggle and an explanatory tooltip. The footer is additionally pinned to the bottom of the list with its reorder arrows disabled, since it renders as page furniture on every page rather than in the body flow.

Preview renders a sample-data PDF through `GET /ws/rest/v1/patientdocuments/visitSummary/preview`, so no patient record is opened. It saves the current settings first, so the preview reflects unsaved toggle and order changes. Fetch failures are surfaced distinctly: a missing `Get Global Properties` privilege shows a permissions message with no retry, an outdated or missing module is reported as such, and other failures show a retryable error.

title: (fix) Pin swr to 2.2.5 to match the app shell and avoid share-scope skew
body: ## Requirements - [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including a conventional commit label. - [ ] My work is based on designs - [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests. ## Summary `swr` is shared as a Module Federation singleton across the O3 frontend. This app declared it as a caret range, which floated up to `2.3.3`, while the app shell (`@openmrs/esm-app-shell`) and most apps (including `openmrs-esm-patient-chart`) pin `swr` exactly to `2.2.5`. With two `swr` minor versions in the shared scope, singleton resolution binds consumers by container init order. `swr/immutable` and `swr/infinite` at 2.3.3 bind against the shell's eager `swr/_internal` at 2.2.5, so `SWRGlobalState.get(cache)` returns `undefined` and the patient chart crashes on render (`TypeError: undefined is not iterable`), intermittently failing distro e2e runs. Pinning `swr` to `2.2.5` aligns these apps with the app shell and removes its contribution to the skew. ## Screenshots ### Consistent undefined is not iterable error in Playwright trace ## Related Issue ## Other Resolves the intermittent patient chart crash seen in distro e2e runs (Module Federation `swr` share-scope skew). Part of a coordinated set of pins across the apps that had floated to 2.3.3; canonical PR: openmrs/openmrs-esm-billing-app#757.

body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/docs/frontend-modules/contributing.en-US#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [x] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

Migrates admin-tools's test runner from jest to vitest across all three workspace packages, aligning the repo with the patterns adopted in [openmrs-esm-patient-management#2532](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-management/pull/2532) and [openmrs-esm-patient-chart#3301](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-chart/pull/3301).

### Layout

- `tools/vitest.shared.ts` holds the actual config: jsdom, `identity-obj-proxy` for css/scss, the `@openmrs/esm-framework -> /mock` alias (exact-match regex so the `/mock` subpath isn't captured), the `@tools/*` and `@mocks/*` path aliases, `setupFiles`, the 80% coverage thresholds, and the `inline: [/@openmrs/]` server-deps hint. `process.env.TZ = 'UTC'` is set at config-load time so the test scripts can drop `cross-env`.
- Root `vitest.config.ts` is a one-line re-export of the shared config.
- Each package gets its own `vitest.config.ts` doing `mergeConfig(sharedConfig, {})`, plus `vitest` as a devDependency. With this in place, ``cd packages/<app> && yarn test`` works without bouncing through the workspace root.

### Root deps

- Drop `jest`, `@swc/jest`, `jest-cli`, `jest-environment-jsdom`, `@types/jest`.
- Add `vitest`, `@vitest/coverage-v8`, `jsdom`.
- Bump `@testing-library/dom` (10.1 -> 10.4), `@testing-library/jest-dom` (6.4 -> 6.8), `@testing-library/react` (15 -> 16) so the `/vitest` subpath of `@testing-library/jest-dom` is available.
- Bump `cross-env` (7.x -> 10.x).

### Setup

`tools/setup-tests.ts` loads `@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest`, swaps every `jest.*` for `vi.*` (scrollIntoView/requestSubmit/matchMedia spies), and rewrites the `ResizeObserver` mock as an ES class. vitest's `vi.fn().mockImplementation(...)` is not constructable, so React's effect-time `new ResizeObserver(...)` call would otherwise fail.

### Per-package scripts

`cross-env TZ=UTC jest --config jest.config.js ...` becomes plain `vitest run --passWithNoTests` / `vitest watch`.

### Test files (9)

- `jest.*` -> `vi.*` throughout.
- `as jest.Mock` casts replaced with `vi.mocked(fn)`, which preserves the real signature. Where the partial mock literal no longer type-checks against the real return type, a single `as unknown as FetchResponse` or `as unknown as ReturnType<typeof usePagination>` keeps the intent at the call site.
- `mockReturnValueOnce({...})` on `openmrsFetch` swapped for `mockResolvedValueOnce({...})` (`openmrsFetch` returns a Promise; the old `as jest.Mock` cast was hiding the mismatch).
- `jest.requireActual` factories rewritten as ``vi.mock(path, async () => ({ ...((await vi.importActual(path)) as object), override }))``.
- `xit` calls in `subscription.test.tsx` rewritten as `it.skip` (`xit` is not a vitest global).
- `jest.mock('./concept-search-results', () => function MockX() {...})` wrapped as `{ default: function MockX() {...} }` so vitest accepts the module-object shape.
- Stale `import '@testing-library/jest-dom'` in `concept-search-input.test.tsx` dropped; the `/vitest` subpath is loaded once from `setup-tests.ts`.
- Carbon's `danger Unsubscribe` button names switched to `/danger\s*Unsubscribe/i`; `@testing-library/react@16` computes the accessible name with an extra space between the icon-only `danger` aria text and the button label.

Root `jest.config.js` and the three per-package `jest.config.js` re-export shims are deleted.
